judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'take such other action as is required of BD pursuant to the Settlement Procedures' is an open-ended residual duty whose content lies outside the four corners of this document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its content depends wholly on the Settlement Procedures incorporated by Section 2.1(b), which are not reproduced here; no contradiction with any visible provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure pass-through delivery obligation keyed to Section 2 of the Auction Agreement; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the preamble's description of the Auction Agreement and with Section 3.1(b)'s express-duties-only limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '.25 of 1% per annum as calculated below' and the adjustment mechanism ('may be adjusted from time to time with the approval of the Company upon a written request of the Broker-Dealer') leave open whether the Company has unfettered discretion to refuse, and the fee is said to be 'for the benefit of the beneficial owners' though owed to the Broker-Dealer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statement that the fee compensates services 'for the benefit of the beneficial owners' pulls against Section 3.1(a) and 5.5, which deny duties or rights to any Person other than the named parties; the payment mechanics are otherwise consistent with 2.5(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An extremely long formula, but each variable is enumerated; the visible flaw is the reference to the definition of 'Broker-Dealer' 'contained in the Series 2004 Auction Bonds' and the daily-period sub-clause (5), which mixes an 'Auction was not held' case into a list of Auction outcomes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(c) locates the 'Broker-Dealer' definition in the Indenture, not in the Bonds, so the two cross-references point to different instruments; the Auction Agent's 'conclusive absent manifest error' calculation also sits against Section 3.1(c)'s negligence standard.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence granting an optional right; 'shall have the right to pay' is clear, though it says nothing about whether payment discharges the Company or creates subrogation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Bond Insurer is not a signatory yet is given rights here and in Sections 5.5 and 5.6(a); whether a non-party can be bound to or benefit from these terms is a whole-instrument question, though 5.5's third-party-beneficiary sentence largely resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The settlement-backstop obligations are specific and the 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' proviso is expressly tied to Section 2.3(d); 'promptly' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 2.6(b)'s disclaimer for the Auction Agent, Trustee, Company and Issuer, and with Section 2.3(d)'s notice mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, broadly worded disclaimer; 'pursuant to the Auction Procedures or otherwise' is a catch-all whose reach beyond the enumerated failures could be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section 2.6(a), which imposes the corresponding obligation on BD alone, so the allocation is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat agency-and-no-duties statement; the words 'solely as agent of the Trustee' and 'owes no duties, fiduciary or otherwise, to any other Person' are about as definite as drafting gets (the missing final period is immaterial).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the many express duties the Auction Agent does owe BD under Sections 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5(b) (holding the fee 'on behalf of the Broker-Dealer'), which is a real, if reconcilable, tension between disclaimed duties and undertaken ones.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard express-duties-only language, tightly cross-referenced to Section 2.1(b); nothing vague to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Section 2.1(b) incorporates the Auction and Settlement Procedures 'in their entirety', the scope of the Auction Agent's 'express' duties turns on an external document, which is a genuine interpretive seam.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences state different standards — no liability 'in the absence of negligence or misconduct', then no liability for good-faith errors of judgment 'unless the Auction Agent shall have been negligent in ascertaining the pertinent facts' — and 'misconduct' is undefined (wilful? any?).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'Section 3.2(d)', a provision not present in the executed text before us, and stands against Section 2.5(b)'s 'conclusive absent manifest error' fee calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) makes the Auction Agent's duty to act depend on 'its judgment' and on 'indemnity satisfactory to the Auction Agent' — subjective standards the parties could contest, though such formulations are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is of a piece with Sections 3.1(a)-(c) and 2.2(b)'s indemnity carve-out; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general standard ('circumstances beyond its reasonable control') followed by an enumerated list introduced by 'including without limitation' — the classic ejusdem generis setting — and the list is cut off mid-sentence in the executed text, leaving the enumeration incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Auction Agent's timing obligations in Sections 2.2 and 2.4 but is consistent with the liability standard in 3.1(c); no direct conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The block names the Issuer as 'HOSPITAL SERVICES CORPORATION' while the first recital defines the Issuer as the 'New Mexico Hospital Equipment Loan Council', and the effectiveness rule speaks of 'the other party' in a three-party agreement — both are namable mechanical defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch is squarely a conflict with the opening recital's definition of 'Issuer' (c001) and with Section 5.5's reference to 'rights expressly granted to the Issuer herein', and only two of the four relevant addressees appear at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The integration clause is unusual in embracing not just this contract but 'the other agreements and instruments executed and delivered in connection with the issuance', an undefined and potentially very large set, which makes the scope of the merger genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 2.1(b)'s incorporation of the Auction and Settlement Procedures and with the Indenture and Auction Agreement referenced in Section 5.10; which of those form part of the 'entire agreement' is not settled by the text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause lists BD, the Bond Insurer and the Auction Agent as the beneficiaries and successors, then excludes all other Persons 'other than the rights expressly granted to the Issuer herein' — an expressio unius list that conspicuously omits the Company, which is a signatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company is a party under the preamble and holds express rights in Sections 2.1(d), 2.3(a) and 2.5, and the Issuer is not a party at all, so the enforcement structure in 5.5 cannot be squared cleanly with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-oral-modification clause; 'each of the parties hereto' plus consent of the Issuer and Bond Insurer is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires consent from the Issuer and Bond Insurer, neither of whom signs, which fits awkwardly with Section 5.5's exclusion of non-parties but is not an outright contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow anti-waiver clause addressed only to 'any subsequent breach'; it says nothing about waiver of the current breach, which is a small but real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(a) requires any waiver to be in a signed writing, which is broader; the two are reconcilable but not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability with no reformation or essential-term proviso; plain and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the agreement qualifies it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts language, definite in every respect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the single execution page; no interaction to worry about.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the United States District Court in the County of New York' misdescribes any existing court (federal districts are not organised by county) and the sentence 'in connection with any such action or proceeding, submit to the jurisdiction' is missing its subject — mechanical errors that go directly to whether the clause is a mandatory federal-forum selection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses forum, so the defect is intrinsic rather than relational, though it bears on Section 5.7 severability if the designated court does not exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause disclaims implied duties only 'on the part of the Company', an asymmetry that invites the argument that implied duties do arise for BD, and it reaches across to the Indenture and Auction Agreement in a one-sentence sweep.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Sections 3.1(a)-(b), which disclaim implied duties for the Auction Agent alone, the instrument protects the Company and the Auction Agent but pointedly not BD, which is exactly the ground on which a BD-duty dispute (see Section 2.3(b)) would be fought.
